pronunciation.approximation: 'mneh-MOH-see-nee' — the first syllable is like 'mneh', the stress falls on the third syllable, and both long vowels are held.

pronunciation.note: Mnēmosýnē is Tier 1: the Greek original contains both length (ē) and acute stress (ý), making it the fullest scholarly restoration. The English 'Mnemosyne' flattens the vowels.

domains.title: Mother of Memory
domains.subtitle: Memory, the Muses, and the Waters of Remembrance
domains.lead: Mnēmosýnē is the personification of memory and the mother of the nine Muses. Without her, there is no poetry, no history, no law, no song. She is the deep reservoir from which all the arts draw, and the spring from which the initiates of the mysteries drink so that they may remember their divine origin after death.

cards.name: Mother of Muses
cards.desc: She and Zeus produced the nine Muses, each presiding over an art or science.

cards.name: Memory Divine
cards.desc: Memory is not merely human recollection but the cosmic retention of all that is.

cards.name: Mystery Spring
cards.desc: Initiates drank from her spring to remember the soul's divine past.

cards.name: Fountain of Song
cards.desc: Poets invoked her so that language would not fail at the moment of making.

symbols.name: Spring or fountain
symbols.meaning: The waters of memory from which the dead must drink.

symbols.name: Book or tablet
symbols.meaning: The written record that preserves what time would erase.

symbols.name: Lamp
symbols.meaning: The light that keeps memory visible in darkness.

symbols.name: Laurel
symbols.meaning: The crown of the poet whose work depends on her gift.

mythology.lead: Mnēmosýnē's myths are few because her function is everywhere. She is the ground of narrative itself.

myths.title: Nine Nights with Zeus
myths.text: Hesiod tells how Zeus lay with Mnēmosýnē for nine consecutive nights in Pieria. From this union came the nine Muses, each bearing a province of the arts. The very number of nights corresponds to the months of gestation, as if memory itself must be incubated before it can give birth to song.

myths.title: The Waters of Memory
myths.text: In Orphic gold tablets buried with the dead, the soul is instructed to avoid the spring of Lēthē (Forgetfulness) and to drink instead from the spring of Mnēmosýnē. By remembering its divine nature, the soul is freed from the cycle of rebirth. Memory, in this tradition, is the key to salvation.

myths.title: Pieria and the Muses
myths.text: Mnēmosýnē was worshipped alongside the Muses in Pieria and on Mount Helicon. She received libations and hymns not as a distant Titan but as the source of all that the Muses dispensed. Without her, the Muses would have nothing to sing.

lore.syncretism: Roman poets identified Mnēmosýnē with Moneta, a title of Juno associated with memory and warning. In the Renaissance she merged with the art of memory, the mnemonic technique by which orators stored speeches in imagined buildings. Modern psychology and neuroscience have taken over the empirical study of memory, but Mnēmosýnē remains the ancient name for the mystery that makes identity possible: the fact that we can recall who we are.
lore.culturalLegacy: Mnēmosýnē lives in every museum (from mouseion, 'place of the Muses') and every act of remembrance. She is invoked at funerals, in national memorials, and in the simple act of telling a story. The word 'mnemonic' derives from her name. In a culture of accelerating forgetting, Mnēmosýnē is the guardian of continuity: she asks us not to let the past dissolve.
lore.extendedMeditation:
Mnēmosýnē is the most quietly powerful of the Titans. She does not fight like Koîos, nor prophesy like Phoebe. She simply remembers. Yet without memory there is no self, no culture, no justice. A people that cannot remember its dead is not a people; a person who cannot remember their promises is not yet a person.

The Orphic instruction is the deepest: when you die, do not drink forgetfulness. Choose memory, even when it hurts. Memory is the link between the soul and the divine. Mnēmosýnē does not promise that the past was good; she promises that it was real, and that reality matters.
lore.originalScriptNote: The Greek is Μνημοσύνη, from μνήμη ('memory'). The initial Mn- cluster is characteristic of Greek words for memory and remembrance. The first and final vowels are long eta (ē), and the stress falls on the antepenult with the acute on -sý-. PUNYCODEX writes Mnēmosýnē with macrons on the long vowels and the acute accent, since the full Greek alphabet is not registrable.
